aliza: Heads-up — saw a regional H100 spot/list price delta in eu-west that changes our committed vs on-demand unit cost by ~12%. Need quick pass on product packaging impact and whether we should accelerate rebalancing reserved SKUs.

matt: Ugh. Which sku/region?

aliza: eu-west1 H100-1 + burst pools. The invoice line item shows a 12% increase effective last billing cycle. Not a transient spot blip — it’s reflected in our committed utilization bills.

jia: Can you paste the billing line?

aliza: Sure — snippet: ```
Resource: GPUs/H100
Region: eu-west1
UnitPrice: $3.45/hr -> $3.86/hr
CommittedDiscount: 25% (applied before bump)
EffectiveUnit: $2.89/hr -> $2.89/hr (commit unchanged)
Net delta on on-demand: +0.41/hr
```

samir: Wait — committed rate stayed same? So our blended unit increases only where we spill to OD or burst. How much spill did we have last month in eu-west?

ella: finance: last month eu-west spill = 18% of total GPU hours (we routed overflow to burst pools). If OD delta is +12% that yields ~2.2% absolute margin hit across the product for eu-west workloads.

matt: 2.2% across product is nontrivial. But packaging changes could mitigate if we shift capacity or adjust routing. What are the levers?

aliza: Levers I can think of: 1) Shift more customers to dedicated/reserved in eu-west (increase commit) 2) Re-route spill to cheaper regions (latency tradeoffs) 3) Backfill with lower-cost quantized instances (if model quality tolerates) 4) Increase price on high-cost SKUs / introduce regional surcharge 5) Absorb short-term and adjust at next pricing review.

jia: Operational constraints: our autoscaler allocs burst in same region first. Cross-region fallback exists but needs opt-in per workload due to data residency/latency. Backfill path to quantized nodes requires model compatibility testing for each model family.

samir: Also note cluster health — we currently have 3 planned maint windows for eu-west next month which will temporarily increase spill. If market prices are higher during those windows, margin squeeze worsens. Suggest we postpone any non-critical maint to avoid synchronized spill + price bump.

ella: From finance POV we can model two scenarios quickly: 
- Scenario A: absorb and keep packaging 
- Scenario B: move 10% of spill into new reserved commit (12 month) in eu-west 
- Scenario C: route 50% spill to us-central (add latency tiering)

ella: Rough back-of-envelope numbers: 
```
Baseline monthly GPU hours (eu-west): 60k hrs
Spill 18% -> 10.8k hrs
OD delta +0.41/hr -> incremental cost = 10.8k * 0.41 = $4,428/month
If we buy 10% more reserved (6k hrs/month) at committed price -> saves ~0.41/hr * 6k = $2,460/month
```

matt: So buying commitment covers ~55% of the incremental cost, but commits are sticky — need to look at utilization profile. Also commitments cost capital and reduce flexibility.

aliza: Right. Also packaging: if we add a small regional surcharge for eu-west heavy customers, we can avoid changing commits. But that’s product friction.

jia: Ops note: cross-region routing to us-central shows median latency increase ~40ms for our common endpoints; P95 hits 120ms for some customers. For chat workloads that might be acceptable, but for real-time features it is not. We need per-customer routing policy.

samir: Proposal: short-term (30d) — 1) postpone non-critical eu-west maint 2) add temporary aggressive backoff to reduce non-essential background jobs in eu-west during peak 3) finance to model commit top-ups for 6/12 months. Medium-term (90d) — evaluate regional surcharge vs commit purchase vs quantization campaign.

ella: I'll run a commit sensitivity table (6/12/24mo) and post numbers. If the incremental delta stays ~4.4k/month it might justify a modest 12mo top-up for predictability.

aliza: Can you include a blended unit econ view by customer tier? We want to know if PLG free-tier is causing disproportionate spill.

ella: Yep — will break out by plan.

matt: Ops: samir/jia, can you prioritize quick perf tests for backfill quantized nodes for the top 3 models this week? If quality hits >98% baseline we can consider 20% backfill.

jia: On it. I'll post results by EOD Friday.

samir: I'll reschedule non-critical maint windows and add a runbook: if OD delta >10% trigger commit-purchase approval flow.

aliza: Thanks — once finance posts the sensitivity table we can decide whether to purchase a small 12mo top-up or toggle region routing. 

ops-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-492 eu-west pricing-anomaly, assignees: samir, ella

matt: Thanks team. Keeping this thread for decisions — please reply with final numbers. :thumbsup:
